history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V20 scored workload, mode, job count, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability ruling, acceptance decision, attribution metric, external-suite boundary, exact-parent contract, and publication boundary. It retains the V20 zig-js-only no-JIT required-bytecode rows, re-pins their runner, and adds exact Context-owned adaptive-binary attribution. No historical scored or accepted report is rewritten. Any later workload, option, checksum, mode, runner, quickening contract, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Re-pins the comparison runner and adds exact hit/miss/dequickening attribution for the non-scored V20 required-bytecode/no-JIT arithmetic profile; every scored field remains unchanged.

context_lifecycle_integration.publication_boundary: This remains the V19 zig-js-only cold lifecycle profile. V21 changes only the runner hash to expose Context-owned quick-binary attribution in separate tier rows; no lifecycle option, scenario, checksum, telemetry, or evidence ruling changes.

quick_binary.publication_boundary: Counters are exact Context-owned atomics read only in the separate attribution mode. Stable Number rows must hit without misses; per-site unit tests prove polymorphic/coercive sites become terminal generic and that one specialized miss dequickens without replay. Exact-parent timing remains a separate artifact.

no_jit_integration.timed_boundary: One invocation in one persistent production Context after ten reduced-work warmups; source/configuration, warmup, Context creation/destruction, attribution, and hardware snapshots are outside elapsed_ns.
no_jit_integration.publication_boundary: These rows freeze logical work and prove required-bytecode/no-native execution. Battery diagnostics and structural attribution are not performance evidence. A speed claim requires exact-parent, order-balanced, quiet-reference AC samples with stable required counters and unchanged controls.
